text:
Business idea lifecycle

Example idea: Create a customer service portal that lets customers submit and track cases while agents manage work efficiently. Each stage refines the idea, reduces risk, and supplies evidence or inputs to the next stage.

End-to-end progression
flowchart TD
    A[Business idea: Customer service portal] --> B[Discovery: Interview customers and agents, map current workflows, identify pain points, test value, and define success measures]
    B --> C[Requirements: Specify user journeys, roles, case rules, integrations, security, audit, performance, and acceptance criteria]
    C --> D[Solution design: Define architecture, data model, interfaces, user experience, identity controls, observability, and deployment approach]
    D --> E[Planning: Prioritize an MVP, split work into increments, estimate effort, assign ownership, identify dependencies, and manage risks]
    E --> F[Development: Build tested vertical features such as case submission, assignment, status tracking, notifications, and reporting]
    F --> G[Testing: Verify units, integrations, workflows, security, accessibility, performance, recovery, and stakeholder acceptance]
    G --> H[Release: Approve the tested version, document changes, prepare support and training, confirm rollback, and schedule launch]
    H --> I[Deployment: Promote the release through controlled environments, migrate data, configure production, verify health, and enable users]
    I --> J[Operations: Monitor reliability, security, usage, and service levels while handling support, incidents, backups, and maintenance]
    J --> K[Continuous improvement: Analyze feedback and metrics, identify new needs, prioritize enhancements, and feed them into discovery]
    K --> B
